formulations.Notes: Self-standing, transparent film. FT-IR C=O stretch curve fitting: free C=O 45% (1755 cm-1), Li+-interacting C=O 55% (1721 cm-1). Transference number was not reported for LiTFSI at 20 mol%.

formulations.Reference: Y. Tominaga, K. Yamazaki, V. Nanthana, J. Electrochem. Soc. 162 (2) A3133-A3136 (2015)

formulations.Notes: PEC purified by chloroform/methanol reprecipitation, dried 60 °C vacuum 24 h. Li-ion conductivity (t+ x sigma) at 80 °C read from Figure 3: log sigma_Li ≈ -5.1 (≈7.9e-6 S/cm); total ionic conductivity not stated in text.
formulations.Reference: Y. Tominaga, K. Yamazaki, V. Nanthana, J. Electrochem. Soc. 162 (2) A3133-A3136 (2015)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: The poly(ethylene carbonate) was about 95% carbonate units and 5% ethylene oxide units in the main chain (by NMR). formulations.Transference notes: Measured by the Bruce-Vincent method (DC polarization at 10 mV plus AC impedance) in a Li|electrolyte|Li cell; steady state reached after about 24 h. formulations.Reference: Y. Tominaga, K. Yamazaki, V. Nanthana, J. Electrochem. Soc. 162 (2) A3133-A3136 (2015)

formulations.Transference notes: Bruce-Vincent method (DC polarization, 10 mV, plus AC impedance) in a Li|electrolyte|Li cell at 80 °C. The value of about 0.23 was read off the Figure 1 plot and is approximate. The text says t+ for LiClO4 fell with rising concentration to below 0.3.
formulations.Notes: Transparent, self-standing film. Li-ion conductivity (sigma_Li = t+ x sigma) at 80 °C was about 10^-5.2 S/cm, read off Figure 3; this is not the total ionic conductivity. For LiClO4, sigma_Li peaked at 40 mol%.
formulations.Reference: Y. Tominaga, K. Yamazaki, V. Nanthana, J. Electrochem. Soc. 162 (2) A3133-A3136 (2015)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Poly(ethylene carbonate) with ~95% carbonate units and ~5% ethylene oxide units in main chain (NMR). [Li+]/[EC unit] = 20 mol% (1/5). Self-standing transparent film.
formulations.Transference notes: Evans-Vincent-Bruce DC polarization (10 mV) + AC impedance, Li|electrolyte|Li cells, steady state after ~24 h. Value read from plot (Fig. 1/Fig. 2), approximate.
formulations.Notes: Li-ion conductivity sigma_Li (= t+ x sigma) at 80 C: log sigma_Li ~ -5.4 (plot reading, Fig. 3). FT-IR: free C=O fraction 61% (1750 cm-1), interacting C=O 38% (1718 cm-1).

formulations.Transference notes: Measured by the combined DC polarization and AC impedance method (Evans–Vincent–Bruce) in a Li|electrolyte|Li cell at 80 °C with 10 mV applied and steady state after about 24 h. formulations.Notes: Salt concentration is 40 mol% Li per EC monomer unit (Li:monomer = 0.4). Li-ion conductivity σLi (= t+ × σ) at 80 °C is log σLi ≈ -4.6 (Figure 3), i.e. σLi ≈ 2.5e-5 S/cm. For LiClO4 and LiBF4, σLi was highest at 40 mol%. FT-IR C=O band: free C=O 34% at 1751 cm-1 and Li-interacting C=O 66% at 1723 cm-1 (Table I).
formulations.Reference: Y. Tominaga, K. Yamazaki, V. Nanthana, J. Electrochem. Soc. 162 (2) A3133-A3136 (2015)

formulations.Transference notes: Bruce-Vincent method (DC polarization 10 mV + AC impedance, Li|electrolyte|Li cells, steady state after ~24 h). Value is approximate, read from a plot in Fig. 1 (~0.16). The paper says LiBF4 t+ values fell gradually below 0.3 as concentration increased.
formulations.Notes: Li-ion conductivity sigma_Li (= t+ x sigma) at 80 °C, read from a plot in Fig. 3: log sigma_Li ≈ -4.6 (≈2.5e-5 S/cm). This is not total ionic conductivity. FT-IR C=O band: 43% free C=O at 1750 cm-1 and 57% interacting (C=O...Li+) at 1724 cm-1.
formulations.Reference: Y. Tominaga, K. Yamazaki, V. Nanthana, J. Electrochem. Soc. 162 (2) A3133-A3136 (2015)

The electrolyte is a transparent, self-standing film. Li salt concentration is 60 mol% relative to EC monomer units ([Li+]/[EC] = 0.6).
formulations.Transference notes: Measured by combined DC polarization (10 mV) and AC impedance (Bruce-Vincent method) on Li|electrolyte|Li cells at 80 °C; steady state after about 24 h. formulations.Polymer system Notes: Poly(ethylene carbonate) from CO2/epoxide copolymerization. About 95% carbonate units and about 5% ethylene oxide units in the main chain (by NMR). Purified by reprecipitation from chloroform into methanol.
formulations.Transference notes: Bruce-Vincent method: DC polarization (10 mV) plus AC impedance on Li|electrolyte|Li cells, steady state after about 24 h. The text says t+ was 'relatively high, above 0.4'; 0.41 is read from Fig. 1. t+ drops sharply at higher LiPF6 concentrations.
formulations.Notes: LiPF6 at 5 mol% relative to EC units ([Li+]/[EC] = 1/20). Self-standing film; the LiPF6 films were slightly opaque. Li-ion conductivity (t+ x sigma) at 80 C read from Fig. 3: log sigma_Li about -5.0 (about 1e-5 S/cm). FT-IR shows LiPF6 dissociates poorly in PEC.
formulations.Reference: Y. Tominaga, K. Yamazaki, V. Nanthana, J. Electrochem. Soc. 162 (2) A3133-A3136 (2015)

formulations.Polymer system Notes: Commercial poly(ethylene carbonate), Mn = 3.7x10^4. Purified by dissolving in chloroform, precipitating in methanol, then vacuum drying at 60 °C for 24 h. By NMR, about 95% of main-chain units are carbonate units and the rest are ethylene oxide units. Salt: LiPF6 at [Li+]/[EC unit] = 20 mol% (Li:monomer = 0.2).
formulations.Transference notes: Approximate value read from Figure 1 plot (not printed). Bruce-Vincent method, DC polarization (10 mV) combined with AC impedance on Li|electrolyte|Li cells; steady state after about 24 h. For LiPF6, t+ fell sharply as salt concentration increased (above 0.4 at 5 mol%).
formulations.Notes: LiPF6 electrolytes were slightly opaque, self-standing films. Li-ion conductivity (t+ x sigma) at 80 °C, read from Figure 3, is log sigma_Li ≈ -5.9 (≈1.3e-6 S/cm). This is not the total ionic conductivity, so it is not reported as a conductivity point.
formulations.Reference: Y. Tominaga, K. Yamazaki, V. Nanthana, J. Electrochem. Soc. 162 (2) A3133-A3136 (2015)

formulations.Transference notes: Bruce-Vincent method (DC polarization 10 mV + AC impedance, Li|electrolyte|Li, steady state after about 24 h). Value (~0.17) read off Figure 1, so it is approximate. The text says t+ for LiPF6 fell sharply from above 0.4 at 5 mol% as concentration increased.
formulations.Notes: Self-standing film; LiPF6 electrolytes were slightly opaque. FT-IR C=O band: 60% free C=O (1742 cm-1) and 40% interacting C=O...Li+ (1720 cm-1), suggesting low LiPF6 dissociation.
